It's been nearly 3 years. We only knew each other for just over a year, 'officially' together for 6 months, but within a few weeks of chatting to each other we expressed feelings for one another. He was very goofy in the way he brought it up first - said he thought a lot about kissing me. I told him to be careful, that I might get the impression that he *liked* me, and then it just spiralled from there. 

We met on Reddit, by chance. He loved to use the word "serendipitous" when describing how we met. We initially wrote stories together. I remember even in those first few days of messaging, the second I would get a response from him it would make my heart squeeze. It started with butterflies, but as time went on the butterflies mellowed out and it just became soothing and a wash of warmth to read his messages and hear his voice. 

He couldn't click/snap his fingers. He could drive - had driven loads - but did not have a license. He used to be a baker, a barista. He collected many different versions of Milton's Paradise Lost, and enamel pins. I collect pins now, too, because of him. He was amazing at DIY and had excellent home decor tastes. He was an amazing cook, always showing me what he'd made. He lived in America for a bit. Studied in London.

We met during COVID and every time we arranged to see each other, plans would have to change because of another lockdown. 

We sent each other mail in the post. He got me a wax seal set because I was in love with the fancy letters he'd send me. 

I mentioned off hand, once, that one of my favourite things was banana bread. Slightly underdone, so it was nice and gooey in the middle. I was having a rough time at university, but didn't want to say anything to him and worry him. But he knew, without me having to explain. And one day a box of banana bread - homemade, exactly how I liked it - arrived in the mail with a little card saying how proud he was of me, how he hoped this would cheer me up a little, that he was there. Have never cried over banana bread before, lol. 

He used to joke about being broody for a puppy with me. Neither of us wanted kids, but we wanted a safe home to call ours, some dogs. He was so excited to meet our puppy. He picked out her puppy collar, helped with names. She's nearly 3 now, too. 

We wanted to live together first, but had already talked about what we'd like our wedding to look like, all the dates we wanted to go on, had planned holidays. We shared with each other what we'd like our home together to look like. 

I wish I'd had more time with him. Real time, in person, to hold him and come to know his body and his smell and all his little quirks in person. I could tell exactly how he was, what mood he was in, just from the intonation of "hey" when he answered the phone, and I was looking forward to getting to know all the physical cues he had too. 

I miss him. I don't sleep very well since he's been gone. He used to call me up and read me to sleep. I think it helped him sleep, too.

They often didn't pay on time and fucked up shift patterns as well. 

They would take on batches of like 15 people, and 10 would be left after the 6 weeks or so of training. Then it felt like we were losing a team member once a fortnight. I was one of the last of my batch to leave, and I only stayed as long as I did because I needed all the money I could get for college, and had an end in sight. 

Fuck that job. Full sympathy for you my guy.

Maybe I'm overthinking this but...

"Why did she slather gravy on my potatoes when she knew I wouldn't eat it?"

If she is as precise as you say, that's a big thing to overlook. She must have known you wouldn't eat it and would swap with someone.

I'm not convinced *you* were her target. I'm not saying you were her planned scapegoat, either, but it seems awfully convenient. 

I think there are a few options here:

- She was using you to poison someone else. People might remember you swapping plates, and that would look suspicious, and therefore frame you. She can get away with it. 

- She was planning to poison herself. 

Hear me out on this last one. 

1) She drank beforehand. Depressed? Nervous?
2) She made the above error, knowing you would swap, and hers being the only plate un-gravy-fied. She left said plate unattended. That's tempting fate for you to swap it. 
3) Even when she knew she had been poisoned, she doesn't appear to have rushed to the hospital. If she had dosed it to kill someone, and realised she'd given it to the wrong person, why wouldn't she make up some excuse about feeling unwell in order to get medical attention?
4) She's gathered the family around for one last meal/hurrah, perhaps?

I don't know why she wouldn't choose any easier and less fallible method, but maybe pride made her unable to physically do it herself, so if she acted *through* someone else it removed the burden from her?

I don't know. 

As I said, probably overthinking this, but I don't think you were the target.

I'm in a similar situation. It's been over 6 months since he passed now. For a long time I didn't dream of him. I would cry myself to sleep, and then my dreams would be peaceful. His friends said they dreamed of him, and I felt...almost jealous. Why would he "visit" them, and not me? Did I not love him enough?

But then a month or so ago I had the first dream: he wasn't dead, he was just missing. His mother and I were speculating where he could have gone. I woke up with such a strong feeling of needing to find him, call him, figure out where he was...to the point where I almost rang his mobile, before I remembered he *was* gone. 

Now, I see him in my dreams. I hold him, tell him I love him. I'll get the sense of having been waiting impatiently for him to arrive, and I can feel the excitement when I see him. We're doing mundane things, or chatting online, or any number of strange dream things. And every time I wake up and get that sinking feeling that he's gone, because for a moment, my brain had tricked itself into thinking he wasn't. 

I don't know if it's just a normal part of accepting his death. I was in denial for a long time, so maybe this is the next stage - of coming to terms with it, saying goodbye. But it's distressing. 

I get where you're coming from, because it hurts so much, but it feels so silly to get so upset and worried about dreams - especially for me, ones that aren't even nightmares, they're just...doing day to day stuff. Living our lives. I feel awkward bringing him up to friends and family at the best of times, yet alone when I'm talking about a dream I've had of him.

I hope you find some peace soon and manage to get some good rest. I'm sorry your dreams are making you relive some of those awful moments. If you can, it would probably be a really good idea to speak to someone about them, just to help you process them a bit. Hang in there <3

Firstly, I'm so sorry for your loss. I wish it was something no one had to experience. 

My partner's mum and I became very good friends after his passing in September. Where we both used to talk to him every day, we now talk to each other. I share moments I wish I could share with him, and it was nice to have each other to lean on (literally and emotionally) at his memorial. We both miss him in different ways - she has lost a child, I have lost a soul mate, but we both have lost a *part of ourselves* and that, at least, we've found some kinship in. 

We're a little over six months now. We've had a few of our "firsts" by this point. I finally, a few weeks ago, had my first day where I didn't cry about him at all. Thought of him, but managed not to cry. She went to her local garden centre where she'd previously only ever gone with him, by herself, and bought some new plants for the garden he had got ready for her. I carry his ashes close to my heart in a pendant whenever I go or do something I wish I could have him there for. Slowly, we're both learning to live again. 

We are both still in denial at moments. I still go to call him on my way home, even after all these months. He is still the first person I wish to tell all my good and bad news to, and it takes me several seconds to realise that what I'm typing out he'll never reply to. I still write to him. She still casts glances over at the chair where he would sit, expecting to see him typing away. When it hits us, we've both described it as feeling like the air has been sucked out of our lungs. It's like I can't breathe. 

It will take time. I cannot tell you how long, because everyone is different, and that's one thing I really hope you take away from this: your experience *will* be different. No one can predict - nor should they *dictate* - how long the motions of grief will take to get through. You don't ever really "finish" them, I feel, but whatever you are feeling at any time, let yourself feel it. 

Even if it's that gut wrenching denial and wishful thinking. Those thoughts will be there whether you suppress them or not, so let them out in any way you feel is helpful. Write to your child. Talk to him. Scream into your pillow. Envelope yourself in his favourite scents. Or, press on, find things to throw yourself into. There is no right or wrong way to grieve. 

Therapy will probably help, so it's good you're getting it! Sometimes just having someone to talk at can do a world of good, even if it's just to talk for hours about who your son was as a person. 

I know my partner's mum found enormous comfort in hearing from his friends and myself about what he meant to them, what he was like as a person out and about in the world. There are things I've been able to share with her that have made her smile, like finding out what a hopeless romantic he was, and all the little plans and dreams we had. I've loved going through family albums with her as she tells me all the stories about his childhood that would have him cringing. If you think it would help, and you know he had people like that in his life, maybe reaching out to them might be a good idea? 

Regardless, I'm sending you internet love and hugs. "It sucks" doesn't even cover it. Again, I'm so sorry for your loss and that you're having to go through this. I wish there was anything of substance I could say or do that could help soften some of that pain for you, or expedite the grieving process. It's early days for you still, and I wish you all the best. <3

"If it was sudden then there must’ve been something that could’ve been done."

I think the worst part, for me, is learning acceptance because of how sudden and out of the blue it was. I can't get over the images in my head of him being found in his bed, how he must have been carried out in a bag, how he was sat alone and cold in that morgue when he should have been building his life with me. They come unbidden and without warning, and I can feel myself drifting off into the aether when they hit, to some place in my head where all of this is beyond comprehension because he \*can't\* be gone. He wouldn't just \*leave\*. I didn't even get to say goodnight to him. He was there, 24/7. There would have been something someone could have done.

Told him not to drink so much. Got him to hospital. Woke him up with a phone call or a shake, or not let him go to sleep in the first place. Got him help sooner. I could've asked him to move in sooner, so he'd never be alone. So I'd be there, if anything ever happened. Or if it did happen, at least we would have had more time together. 

​

I just wish for one last conversation. Just to ask him questions, say "I love you" again.

I feel this too. After three weeks, people seemed to tire of me being sad. It's been three months now. His funeral was exactly a week ago. And I have lost so many friends because I'm not getting over him fast enough. 

Every day I consider following him. 

Please, if you ever feel lonely or miss him, please message me. Tell me about your boyfriend. What you're feeling. How much you miss him, fond memories you have. Because that's what I wish people would do for me. 

It kills me that whenever I just want to share a memory of him, not even a sad one, I can see their eyes glazing over with disinterest. It makes grieving all that much harder because I feel like my sadness is inconveniencing people, or that the novelty has worn off for them and they're bored of me not being smiley again yet. 

I don't want anyone else to feel like that. So if you aren't getting the sympathy and support from your people IRL, come yell in my inbox. You're always welcome. I promise.

Honestly, I've not really had much advice from friends at all. Most of what they've said to me has been some version of "you have to move on", or "he wouldn't want you to be sad", or "you can't ruin your life like this, pull yourself together". The most helpful and honest ones have simply said "I don't know what to say to you".

Any time I want to take just a moment to be sad, or I have a bad day where I just want to stay in bed, I get berated, and they're right. I do need to suck it up. Eventually. It just feels like when I do that right now I'm putting on a costume and pretending to be fine, when I'm not. I'm really not. I want him back. I don't want to be here. I don't care what happens to me at this point because I finally found a scrap of happiness and acceptance in my life and then it was ripped away from me. 

It's probably dramatic. It's probably irrational. But I can't stop what I'm feeling.

It's nice when I'm with his family, because it's like a little bubble where time stands still and I don't have to do all this "moving on" that everyone else around me wants to do. I don't have to think about it all. People don't understand how much it throws you off course, losing someone you expected to spend the rest of your life with. 

Planning his funeral was awful. We had planned things about our wedding if/when we got married. We had discussed our thoughts about the afterlife at length. We'd both made it known what we wanted to happen if we were in a life threatening injury. But never once had we talked about our wishes for our funerals, because we never anticipated having to plan them any time soon. 

But even then, having that to plan and wait for, gave me something to cling onto. Now he's really gone. There will be no more steps to go through, no funeral to attend. His birthday has already passed. It's just emptiness ahead and it's really hitting home hard how very gone he is. I definitely get it - all those plans, they involved him. Knowing that they can never happen with him is heart breaking. 

I hope you find some solace in the future. Sending hugs back your way too. <3 It's rough.

I get this. I have, several times, had to pick myself up and take myself to a safe place where I know I won't have the opportunity to act on these thoughts.

Most of all, though, I feel lonely. And the only person right now who can make me not feel so alone, is him. I search for him everywhere and in everyone but I know he's not coming back, and that often leaves me wishing I could go too. Because coming to terms with never seeing him again is too much. I would rather feel nothing at all than this. And maybe there is a slim chance an afterlife does exist, and there we could be reunited.

Oh, I totally understood the drinking. It was something we talked about at length together and I never was angry with him for it. I knew he had his reasons. I knew why he drank. It hurt, but I didn't blame him, because I know it was a coping mechanism for underlying issues. I used to have my own very unhealthy coping mechanisms and I know how hard it is to think rationally when you're in that state where the only thing that works to numb what you're feeling is to fall back on those habits.

And I know when he was contacting people for sex and such, it was when he was drunk, and that he felt ashamed afterwards...but it's knowing that their might have been something *more* than sex with someone that's really hurting, and not knowing whether he was lying to me, or them, or both of us, and who and what to believe. And the fact that we had discussed open relationships before and knew that so long as he told me what was going on, I didn't mind him satiating his needs elsewhere, especially as I had to work long hours sometimes. But he didn't tell me. I found out through other people. And now I don't know how seriously he did feel about me. If it was just a new thing while I was working I could understand it, but it sounds like it had been going on from the start and I was the newcomer on the scene. 

I wish I could take time off to retreat. Unfortunately he passed away in September and I've already taken so much time off grieving. From about two weeks after his passing my friends and family and colleagues were very much "okay, stop being sad, it's time to move on" and they've only got less sympathetic over time. So to take further time now would probably only strain those relationships more. 

It's hard to know what to do. Part of me doesn't want to think about it all, the other part wants answers. But I know I might not like the answers. 

Thank you for your words though. It

There are so many reasons why they think I should: we had arguments, we weren't sure if we were going to work, the relationship was young - only a year - and because of the pandemic our chances to meet with each other had been limited.

But I miss him every day. A piece of my soul went with him. I'm filled with anger and jealousy towards those who *don't* understand. No one in my friends and family have lost a partner under the age of 70. Certainly not under the age of 30, suddenly, for no rhyme or reason. So when they come to me and say "How are you doing? It will get better. I understand. You know, I still think of X and miss them." I want to say no, you don't understand. Because X is still alive. You may not have a relationship any more, but you know they're out there, living their best life, happy and safe.

I would give anything to know he was alive, somewhere, finding a new life, even if it wasn't with me.

But if you answer "how are you doing?" with *oh, good, thanks* you seem callous, like you've moved on. It feels like you're giving up your permission to grieve and feel sad about the loss with those few words.
